name: Surgical and dental instruments manufacturing

problems.words: Instruments go to five different vendors and we lose track of where a lot is
quick_ideas: List every lot currently out with vendors, with stage and date sent, so you have one picture today
Mark which lots are tied to the nearest shipment, so you chase those first

workzap_build.text: A lot tracker following each lot through forging, machining, heat treatment, filing, polishing, passivation and marking, with vendor and dates.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many lots are with vendors at any time?
problems.free_stops: How each stage is recorded and overdue lots flagged is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk through current vendor lots and note each lot's last known stage and send date once, so missing handoffs stand out today.
Give one person one notebook page for every lot sent out, so each vendor handover stays tied to the same lot.

problems.words: Pieces sent to the polisher and pieces returned don't match
quick_ideas: Count the next return in front of the vendor's person, so the count is agreed on the spot
Reconcile what each vendor holds today

workzap_build.text: A vendor issue and receive ledger with counts, shortfalls and payments per stage.

problems.ask_first: Is the mismatch mostly with one polisher, or across all your vendors?
problems.free_stops: How counts are confirmed and tied to payment is covered in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the send note count with the returned tray count for each polishing lot this week, so the mismatch point is pinned down.
Make one person write outgoing and returned piece counts for each polishing lot in one notebook, so disputed numbers have one source.

problems.words: Buyer wants lot-wise records and we build them by hand after the fact
quick_ideas: For the next lot, keep one folder where every stage's date and result is added as it happens, so the record builds itself
Note which documents buyers ask for most

workzap_build.text: A digital batch record built as each stage is completed, exportable per shipment.

problems.ask_first: Which record do buyers ask for most, the material certificate, the inspection result or the process dates?
problems.free_stops: What each record holds and how it is exported is set out in the solution document; regulatory content is for your quality or regulatory adviser.

extra_ideas.text: Note which lot papers are usually rebuilt later and which stage they came from, so the heaviest paperwork gap is obvious.
Give one role the job of placing each lot paper into one folder on the same day, so buyer records gather during production.

problems.words: Rejection rate at final inspection is high and we don't know which stage causes it
quick_ideas: Note the reason for each rejection at final inspection for one week, so a pattern appears
Trace the most common reason back to the stage that causes it

workzap_build.text: An inspection form on the phone recording results per lot and stage, rejection reasons and photos, summarised by stage and vendor.

problems.ask_first: Does the rejection show up more at the finishing stage, or the forging and grinding stage?
problems.free_stops: Inspection points and rejection categories are kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Mark each final inspection rejection by defect type and previous stage for one week, so the stage behind rework starts to show.
Give one inspector one notebook for rejection reasons at final check, so rework discussions use the same evidence each day.

problems.words: Laser marking errors, wrong logo on a private label lot
quick_ideas: Check the marking job sheet against the order once more before the next run, so the logo is right
Keep each buyer's marking instructions in one place

workzap_build.text: A marking job sheet checked against the order and the buyer's item master before marking starts.

problems.ask_first: Does the wrong logo happen with new private-label buyers, or with repeat ones as well?
problems.free_stops: How marking instructions are stored and checked is covered in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare the buyer order sheet with the marking note before the next private label run, so wrong logos are caught earlier.
Assign one person to keep each buyer's current marking instructions together in one place, so the floor uses the latest version.

problems.words: Buyer says shipment short against packing list
quick_ideas: Have a second person recount the next shipment against the packing list before sealing
Note where the last shortage happened

workzap_build.text: A packing list builder with scan-check against the order before boxes close.

problems.ask_first: Is the shortage usually a few pieces on large orders, or whole boxes missing?
problems.free_stops: The scan-check flow is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note the carton packed, packing list line, and final count for the next few shipments, so the shortage point becomes visible.
Give one packer the job of keeping one live packing list at the table during packing, so sealed boxes match what was counted.

problems.words: Certificate renewals and audit dates sneak up
quick_ideas: List every certificate, licence and audit date in one place, so nothing is a surprise
Note who is responsible for each

workzap_build.text: A certificate and audit calendar with reminders well ahead and a document folder.

problems.ask_first: Which comes up most unexpectedly, the certificates, the audits or the licence renewals?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timing and folder structure are kept for the solution document; what each certificate requires is for your regulatory adviser.

extra_ideas.text: List every renewal and audit month on one page and compare it with this quarter, so upcoming documentation pressure is visible.
Assign one role to review the renewals page at the same time each week, so dates stop arriving as last minute surprises.

quick_ideas: List every buyer with what is due and since when
Call or write to the oldest few this week

workzap_build.text: A buyer receivables ledger with ageing and scheduled reminders.

problems.ask_first: Is it a few big buyers who pay months late, or most of them?
problems.free_stops: Reminder schedule and follow-up order are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note each shipped order with shipment date and payment received date once, so the slowest paying buyers are easy to spot.
Give one person one notebook page for all overdue buyer follow ups at a fixed weekly time, so chasing happens routinely.

problems.words: Inquiries from website and B2B platforms aren't followed up
quick_ideas: Gather all open inquiries into one list with date received
Give one person responsibility for first replies

workzap_build.text: An inquiry tracker with reply timers, and an updated digital catalogue searchable by category and catalogue number.

problems.ask_first: Which source brings the most unanswered inquiries, the website or the buyer listing sites?
problems.free_stops: How inquiries flow in and the catalogue is structured are covered in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count open inquiries by source and by days waiting for reply once this week, so the biggest response backlog is clear.
Assign one staff member one list for all new inquiries and one daily reply window, so leads stop sitting unseen.

problems.words: Owner chases each vendor on WhatsApp personally
quick_ideas: Decide which vendor updates you truly need, so others can be handled by staff
Hand vendor follow-up for one stage to one person this week

workzap_build.text: A daily view of every lot by vendor and stage, so follow-up runs from one screen instead of the owner's phone.

problems.ask_first: Which stage do you chase vendors for most, the forging, the polishing or the plating?
problems.free_stops: Who owns which follow-up and how it is escalated is set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many vendor messages only need status collection versus owner judgment this week, so your personal chasing load is clear.
Assign one staff member to collect vendor stage updates in one notebook at one daily time, so replies stop waiting for you.

never_say: Any help falsifying or "arranging" CE, FDA, ISO or other certificates, test reports, markings or batch records.
Any regulatory, sterilisation, clinical-use or material advice; suggest a regulatory or quality adviser.
Anything on acids or chemicals for passivation; chemical burns are emergencies.
Customs, misdeclared goods, origin or value.
Storing vendor, worker, buyer or patient details; if a patient was harmed, point to medical help.
Any guarantee of fewer rejections or faster audits.

sample_reply.person: Our lots go through forging, filing and polishing outside and I never know where they are. Can you help?
sample_reply.pi:
Sure, this can be sorted, and none of it needs special equipment.
First, list every lot currently out with vendors, with its stage and the date it left, so you have one clear picture today.
Second, mark which lots belong to the nearest shipment, so those are chased first.
Workzap could take it further with: a lot tracker that follows each lot through every vendor stage and flags overdue or short returns each day.

Shall I prepare a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
